item.title: A coin nobody asked for
item.description: Tulparcoin landed in everyone's phone last week. What we actually know, in five points. It launched on 22 September. Every registered adult was offered 100 coins for free. The total supply is 900 million coins, and 30% are held by the Forum, the organisation behind it. On 24 September the Bank of…

item.title: Ten kilos of dried apricots
item.description: Why a kilo of dried apricots in January costs what a bucket of fresh ones costs in July, and why that is fair. Dried, an apricot loses about four-fifths of its weight. So ten kilos of fresh fruit make two of dried, plus a week of work on a hot roof, plus the risk of rain. When you pay the winter…

item.title: The remittance queue
item.description: Money from relatives abroad still holds up a lot of Irad's families. A Saturday at a transfer office. On Saturday mornings the transfer office near the bazaar has a queue out of the door. Mostly women, mostly with a telephone in one hand and a passport in the other, waiting for the code from a son…

item.title: The corner shop and the phone
item.description: A QR code from the bank is now taped to every shop counter in Talas. What it changes for the woman behind the counter. I asked the owner of the shop under my building how her business changed since customers started paying by scanning the bank's QR code with their phones. Three things. First, less…

item.title: Bazaar or supermarket?
item.description: I bought the same basket of food at the Bazar-i Kalan and at a Bereke for eight weeks. The answer is "it depends on the onion". The basket: bread, milk, eggs, rice, onions, potatoes, carrots, mutton, sunflower oil, tea, sugar. Eight Saturdays, same list. The bazaar won on vegetables and meat every…

item.title: What a toi really costs
item.description: I added up eleven weddings in Talas and the villages. The hall is not the expensive part. Families tell me the wedding hall is the big cost. In the eleven budgets I collected it was on average less than a fifth. The real money goes on meat, on the gifts both families exchange, on the clothes, and…

item.title: The jam-season sugar mystery
item.description: Why sugar costs more in July, every year, and what a family with a basin of apricots can do about it. Every July half the country makes jam at the same time. Demand for sugar jumps for six weeks, the wholesalers know it, and the price on the shelf rises before the apricots are even ripe. The…

item.title: Why a letter
item.description: Issue one. What this letter is and what it is not. For twelve years I wrote reports that eleven people read. Nine of them were in the same building.
